title: Bram and the Veil
premise: Mara Thornbury's quiet life as a debt-bound scribe shatters when a mute child arrives speaking a dead tongue that only Mara, through her temple training, can half-translate. The child is the vessel of a soul sold to the Undercourt beneath Mount Caelum, and its original owner — a boy named Bram — will be erased forever when the moon completes its thirteenth turn. Hunted by the Veilwardens who enforce the valley's magicless peace, Mara flees with the child and a disgraced hedge-witch named Odile, discovering along the way that her own bloodline is bound to the bargain that sold Bram's soul. In the Undercourt, Mara learns justice there is transactional, not moral, so she cheats it: she offers the court her own name in exchange for Bram's, erasing herself from every record and memory. Bram wakes free; only the child, who keeps one untranslated word meaning 'Mara,' remembers she existed — until Odile finds a loophole in the court's own ledger and writes her back into the world.
about_author: Orsen Fairweather is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing legal documents from defunct monasteries, an experience that left him obsessed with what names and debts do to people. He writes fantasy about ordinary clerks caught in extraordinary bargains from a farmhouse he refuses to geotag.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. We meet Mara copying tithes in the temple of the magicless valley, counting down her debt years with grim patience. A knock at the scriptorium door reveals a child, barefoot in snow, speaking a language no one recognizes. Emotional beat: restless longing cracked open by mystery.

chapters.title: A Word Older Than Kingdoms
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The temple elders want to hand the child to the Veilwardens, but Mara recognizes fragments of the speech in a forbidden pre-kingdom text. The child says one word she can parse: 'Bram.' Emotional beat: forbidden curiosity hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Veil Keeps Out
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A hedge-witch living at the valley's edge explains the Veil: magic cannot cross into the valley, which is why the child was sent here — to hide a soul where the Undercourt cannot reach. Emotional beat: wary alliance forming between two outsiders.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Odile deciphers the child's ramblings: his soul belongs to Bram, sold to the Undercourt, and the child-body will fail when the moon completes its thirteenth turn. Veilwardens arrive at the temple asking questions. Emotional beat: dread and a ticking clock.

chapters.title: The Debt Collector Comes at Dusk
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Warden-Captain Hesk interrogates Mara, revealing the temple itself reported her 'irregularities.' She realizes staying means the child's capture and her own ruin. Emotional beat: betrayal by the institution she served.

chapters.title: Running the Valley Floor
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Mara steals the temple's seal-ring and flees with the child to Odile's cottage; Odile burns her own hedge-charms to mask their trail. Emotional beat: first taste of chosen loyalty over safety.

chapters.title: The Road That Remembers
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The three travel toward the mountain pass; the old road shows them echoes of everyone who ever walked it fleeing something. The child begins speaking more clearly, naming things Bram loved. Emotional beat: grief for a boy they've never met.

chapters.title: Tollhouse of Broken Oaths
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. At a mountain tollhouse, a smuggler named Ferren agrees to guide them past the Wardens' cordon — for a price Mara pays with the stolen seal-ring. Emotional beat: the cost of trust, and the thrill of outmaneuvering power.

chapters.title: Where Magic Pools
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Crossing the Veil's boundary, magic floods back into the world and into Odile, long starved of it. The child reacts violently to raw magic, screaming in Bram's voice. Emotional beat: wonder shadowed by fear of what the child is becoming.

chapters.title: The Shepherd of Hollow Men
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. They shelter with a community of people who traded pieces of themselves to the Undercourt — a man without his courage, a woman without her grief. They warn the price of dealing with the court. Emotional beat: horror at what bargains cost.

chapters.title: Hesk on the Mountain Road
chapters.summary: Hesk's POV. The Warden-Captain, pursuing them, recalls his own sister's soul-debt and begins questioning whom the law actually serves. He lets a crucial clue slip past him deliberately. Emotional beat: a hunter's conscience waking.

chapters.title: The Gate Beneath the Root
chapters.summary: Ferren's POV. The smuggler leads them to the Undercourt's gate inside a hollowed root-system, then abandons them at the threshold, keeping their payment and his conscience separate. Emotional beat: abandonment at the point of no return.

chapters.title: Court of Counted Things
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Inside, the Undercourt is a vast archive where everything — memories, years, names — is filed and tradable. Mara poses as a debt auditor using her scribe skills. Emotional beat: her mundane competence becomes survival.

chapters.title: The Clerk Who Sold a Child
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara finds Bram's contract and discovers the seller's mark: her own grandmother's name. Her family's prosperity was bought with Bram's soul. Emotional beat: identity shattered — she is descended from the villain.

chapters.title: What Odile Buried
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Captured while creating a diversion, Odile bargains with a court magistrate, offering secrets about the Veil's construction to buy time. She learns the court fears loopholes above all things. Emotional beat: sacrifice sharpened into strategy.

chapters.title: Amendment, Forged
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Working nights in the archive, Mara drafts a forged amendment to Bram's contract — but the court's ledgers detect lies. Only a true offer of equal value will hold. Emotional beat: despair giving way to terrible clarity.

chapters.title: The Price of a Name
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara understands the only currency the court cannot refuse: her own name, freely given, erasing her from every record and memory. She signs before she can lose her nerve. Emotional beat: self-sacrifice as the ultimate act of authorship.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Turn, Moonrise
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. As the moon completes its turn, the trade executes: Bram's soul returns to the child, who transforms into a living boy — and Mara vanishes mid-embrace, forgotten even by Odile. Emotional beat: triumph laced with devastation.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Remembered One Word
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Awake and whole, Bram carries one untranslatable residue: a word meaning 'Mara' that no one else can hear or understand. He refuses to let it go. Emotional beat: stubborn love against erasure.

chapters.title: Loophole
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Grieving someone she cannot remember, Odile re-enters the Undercourt and exploits the flaw Mara's forgery planted: the ledger must record what was given, and a given name can be inherited back. Emotional beat: cunning as devotion.

chapters.title: Written Back Into the World
chapters.summary: Bram and Odile's POV. Odile inscribes Mara's name in the court's own ledger with Bram as witness-inheritor; the amendment holds. Mara steps out of blankness into the mountain dawn, remembered at last. Emotional beat: resurrection through found family.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts, Amended
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Home in the valley, Mara's debt annulled by the court's own records, she opens a school for reading dead languages, with Bram her first student and Odile the disreputable neighbor. Hesk looks away, forever. Emotional beat: quiet, earned belonging.
